messages:
alex: heads up — encoder-prod HPA shot to 12 replicas around 08:02 but 5 pods are Pending for >6m. CA didn't add gpu nodes. latency p99 spiked to 3.2s. anyone seeing nodepool provisioning stuck?

maria: can you paste `kubectl get hpa,deploy,po -n inference` and `kubectl describe nodepool gpu-encoder-usw2`?

alex: pasted quick outputs:
```
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference encoder-hpa
NAME         REFERENCE       TARGETS         MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
encoder-hpa  Deployment/enc   600m/200m cpu    3         30        12         2h
```
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep encoder
encoder-7f4   Pending   0/1   ContainerCreating   6m
encoder-9c1   Pending   0/1   Unschedulable       7m
encoder-...  Running   1/1   10m
```
`kubectl describe nodepool gpu-encoder-usw2` shows min=0, max=10, current=0; creation taking ~4m but stuck at provisioning due to quota/image pull?

sam: last week VPA was autoscaling memory for this deployment, clients reported restarts. If VPA is set to `updateMode: Auto` it can bump resources which then makes HPA readjust because CPU/memory targets shift. That plus CA min=0 warm-pool = 0 is a bad combo.

kai: also saw noisy external metrics from prometheus-adapter for `http_requests_rate`. The adapter emits short spikes; HPA reacting to instantRate => rippling scale. We should smooth with a `rollingWindow` or use `rate(query[2m])` with longer window.

alex: infra logs show CA attempted to scale but GCP quota denied the new preemptible nodes: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Insufficient vGPU quota in region us-west2`. So CA aborted. Meanwhile pending pods time out and HPA keeps scaling replicas because metric sustained.

maria: immediate mitigation suggestions:
- set HPA to use smoothed metric: `avg_over_time(http_requests_total[2m])` or use `metric stability window` on adapter.
- flip VPA to `updateMode: "Off"` for this deployment so it doesn't restart pods during the burst. Keep recommender on.
- increase nodepool min to 1 or set a small warm-pool for gpu-encoder-usw2 to avoid cold starts.

sam: +1 on VPA off. Also add `minReadySeconds: 30` on the deployment and `PodDisruptionBudget` to prevent churn during scale-up. That reduces flapping with HPA.

kai: we should also tune CA scale-up behavior: set `--scale-up-delay` smaller for the gpu nodegroup or use cluster-autoscaler expander policy to prefer adding existing gpu pools. And set a nodeGroup-level quota override so CA doesn't try preemptible if quota is low.

infra-bot: incident created: #INC-2025-328 assigned to oncall. Summary: encoder-prod pending pods due to quota + noisy external metric -> HPA overreacting.

alex: short-term action I'll do now: 1) set VPA updateMode Off for encoder deployment, 2) bump nodepool min=1 on gpu-encoder-usw2, 3) open GCP quota request for vGPU + notify capacity. Will post commands.

maria: commands to run:
```
kubectl -n inference patch vpa encoder-vpa --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"updatePolicy":{"updateMode":"Off"}}}'
gcloud container node-pools update gpu-encoder-usw2 --cluster=redwood-prod --region=us-west2 --min-nodes=1
```

sam: after that, follow-up: create a prometheus rule to export `http_requests_rate_smoothed` and point HPA at that metric; add 2m moving average. Long-term: split latency-driven HPA from qps-driven HPA (use two HPAs or rewrite to target request-per-pod stable metric).

kai: long-term: prefer a warm dedicated GPU pool for p99-sensitive workloads (reserved capacity) versus pure preemptible. Also add `external.metric` smoothing and `horizontalPodAutoscaler.stabilizationWindowSeconds` to 300 to avoid chasing spikes.

alex: noted. I'll implement the patches and monitor p99. If CA still fails due to quota, we'll temporarily failover to a lower-q model variant to keep latency SLOs.

maria: thanks. can someone add the final config diffs to the infra repo and link the PR here? :thumbsup:

alex: will open PR and update ticket. tagging @oncall for follow up. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
